text:
Sara L: Heads up — after the RBAC rename we pushed last night I'm seeing sporadic Decrypt failures for restore jobs from the 2023-11 archive bucket. Not mass outage but 6/120 restores failed with AccessDenied from KMS. Anyone else seeing this?
Mike R: saw 2 failures in the canary cluster around 03:13 UTC. Error: \"AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-1234\"
Kim: we renamed the role enc-restore -> enc-restore-v2 and updated most policies, but I didn't touch the KMS grant list. Could be grants referencing the old principal ARN.
Jordan: is this for recent snapshots or older ones?
Sara L: older snapshots (2023-11 through 2024-01) — same CMK used, but the upload path included a service principal that was the old role. Restores that need CreateGrant+Decrypt seem to be failing. New uploads (2025+) are fine.
encops-bot: Detected 6 decrypt failures in restore-service v2 between 2025-11-08T03:10:23Z and 2025-11-08T03:14:01Z. Sample log: 
```
2025-11-08T03:12:11Z restore-service ERROR restore_job=job-4921 decrypt_error=AccessDeniedException
CausedBy: Not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-1234
```

Mike R: quick check I pulled the grants for that key — looks like the grants reference a principal arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/enc-restore (old). After the rename, the role arn changed and grants are now orphaned. AWS grants don't automatically remap.
Kim: ugh. So restores that rely on the grant fail because the grantee principal doesn't exist anymore. We intentionally didn't rotate CMKs.
Jordan: mitigation options: 1) recreate grants for enc-restore-v2 with equivalent constraints, 2) add temporary inline policy to allow kms:Decrypt for the new role (short-lived), or 3) re-run restores from a node with the old principal (hard).
Mike R: I can create an immediate CreateGrant call scoped to the specific grant ID for the duration of the restore window. Something like: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id abcd-1234 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/enc-restore-v2 --operations Decrypt --name temporary-restore-grant
```
This returns a GrantId — but remember grants have retiring principals and must be tracked.
Kim: agree. Need to check existing grant constraints: some grants were limited to a particular encryptionContext (snapshot_id) — can't just open broad grants. Mike, can you list grants and show constraints for the failing jobs?
Mike R: posted the list for key abcd-1234 (sanitized): 
```
- GrantId: g-1  Grantee: arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/enc-restore  Operations: Decrypt  Constraints: {\"EncryptionContextSubset\": {\"snapshot_id\":\"snap-202311-01\"}}
- GrantId: g-2  Grantee: arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/enc-restore  Operations: Decrypt  Constraints: {}
```

Jordan: if we re-create the grant for enc-restore-v2 we must preserve the EncryptionContextSubset to avoid exposing other snapshots. Good to prefer targeted grants.
Sara L: prioritized action: create targeted grants for affected snapshot_ids (we have 6 failing snapshot ids). Also add a playbook entry to the RBAC rename checklist so this doesn't happen next time.
ops-oncall: I'll approve a short-lived grant creation for those 6 snapshots; please include exact snapshot ids, and set an explicit retirement timestamp 12 hours out.
Mike R: doing the create-grant now for snap-202311-01 and snap-202311-17 (two examples) with encryption context constraint. Command I ran: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id abcd-1234 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/enc-restore-v2 --operations Decrypt --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={\"snapshot_id\":\"snap-202311-01\"} --name temp-restore-snap-202311-01
```
Response: GrantId g-1001.
Kim: after you put the grants in place, can we re-run the failed restores? Please throttle to avoid overload.
Mike R: re-run kicked off, first two succeeded. I'll re-run the rest in batches of 10.
Jordan: longer-term action items: 
- Update RBAC rename runbook to include: list KMS grants referencing role ARNs and re-issue as needed.
- Add an automated audit query that detects KMS grants whose grantee principal no longer exists (or matches an old role regex).
- Consider switching to keyed grant principals (service principals) where possible, or rely on key policy + IAM rather than many per-role grants.
Sara L: also add a governance note: when renaming roles that are used in grants, the operator must either 1) retire and recreate grants or 2) create an alias role mapping and keep the old principal ARN for a 24h propagation window.
encops-bot: Suggested audit query: find-kms-grants-with-missing-principals -> 
```
-- pseudo SQL
SELECT GrantId, GranteePrincipal FROM kms_grants WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM iam_entities WHERE arn = GranteePrincipal)
```

Kim: small security question — are we ok creating temporary grants from a compliance perspective? We need retention of who created them (audit logs) and short TTL.
ops-oncall: fine as long as we: 1) create grants with tight encryption context, 2) set retire_on_date or ensure we call retire-grant, 3) log user and command in incident ticket.
Sara L: I'll open an incident ticket and attach the grant IDs and job ids. Also will add the RBAC rename checklist change to the infra runbooks.
Mike R: FYI I blurred principals and ids in the ticket and linked the CloudTrail events showing CreateGrant and RetireGrant.
Jordan: follow-up: schedule a postmortem to confirm whether any other workloads used the old role for grants (snapshot replication service?).
Kim: +1. Also recommend we add an automated pre-rollout check: \"if rename touches roles that appear in kms_grants, fail the rename or require manual approve.\"
Sara L: thanks all. Current status: 6 failures -> 0 failures after targeted grants and re-runs. Will keep monitoring for 24h. Closing loop once runbook updates are live. :white_check_mark:
